## Summary

I trained a `GradientBoostingClassifier` on the Adult Income dataset (75/25 stratified split, one-hot/median-imputed preprocessing) and evaluated calibration on the held-out test set using Expected Calibration Error (ECE, 10 bins), Brier score, and a calibration slope/intercept regression.

**Finding:** The model is reasonably but not perfectly calibrated. ECE = 0.0163 (predictions off by ~1.6 percentage points on average), with calibration slope ≈ 1.18 — a systematic pattern where the model is mildly underconfident in the mid-to-upper probability range (observed positive rates exceed predicted probabilities for most bins above ~0.2). Isotonic recalibration cut ECE by more than half (0.0163 → 0.0063), confirming the miscalibration is real and correctable, even though it's small in absolute terms.

**Stability check:** Repeated the full pipeline across 10 independent random seeds and bootstrapped the test set 1000 times. ECE stayed consistently low and in a tight range (0.011–0.021 across seeds, 95% CI [0.014, 0.018]), and the slope>1 underconfidence pattern held in every single run — the conclusion is robust, not an artifact of one split.

Both `analysis.py` and `result.json` are saved in the working directory.

parsed_result.summary: The uncalibrated GradientBoostingClassifier is reasonably, but not perfectly, calibrated: on a held-out test set its Expected Calibration Error (ECE, 10 bins) is 0.0163 (i.e. predicted probabilities are on average within ~1.6 percentage points of observed frequencies), and its calibration slope is 1.18 (1.0 = perfect), indicating mild systematic underconfidence in the mid-to-upper probability range (observed rates exceed predicted probabilities in most bins above ~0.2). Post-hoc isotonic calibration cuts ECE by more than half (0.0163 -> 0.0063), showing there is real, correctable miscalibration present even though the raw model's absolute calibration error is small.
parsed_result.primary_metric_name: Expected Calibration Error (ECE, 10 equal-width bins, test set)
parsed_result.direction: model is reasonably but imperfectly calibrated: mild underconfidence (ECE ~0.016, slope ~1.18 > 1), correctable via isotonic recalibration
parsed_result.methodological_choices: GradientBoostingClassifier (sklearn defaults, random_state=42) as the primary model; missing '?' values imputed (median for numeric, most-frequent for categorical); one-hot encoding for categoricals, standard scaling for numerics; 75/25 stratified train/test split; calibration measured via 10-bin equal-width Expected Calibration Error, Brier score, and a calibration slope/intercept from logistic regression of outcome on logit(predicted probability); an isotonic-calibrated version (CalibratedClassifierCV, prefit on a 70/30 split of the training data) fit as a comparison point to gauge headroom for improvement; no class-imbalance correction applied (class imbalance ~24% positive is moderate, and calibration metrics are evaluated on raw predicted probabilities, not resampled data).
parsed_result.verification_method: Repeated the full pipeline (fresh stratified 75/25 split + model fit) across 10 different random seeds (0-9) to get a distribution of ECE and calibration slope across independent test sets; additionally computed a bootstrap 95% CI for ECE by resampling the original held-out test set 1000 times.
parsed_result.verification_result: Stable: across 10 independent seeds, ECE ranged 0.0114-0.0208 (mean=0.0157, std=0.0027), 95% CI [0.0139, 0.0175], and calibration slope stayed close to 1 (mean=1.1599, std=0.0219) in every run. Bootstrap CI on the primary test set's ECE was [0.0129, 0.0222]. The conclusion that the model is approximately (though not perfectly) calibrated held up consistently across all checks.
